title: Recipe 62 — Response ratings: rate → distill → eval → optimize

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “A thumbs-down is worth nothing on its own. This recipe is the path from one thumbs-down to a measured improvement.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — nothing committed is touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — distilling with --judge is billed.

groups.title: Beat 1 · a harness that collects ratings

beats.label: Type the recipe's rated channel
beats.cue: “A channel bot, because ratings need real users. The feedback block is the only unusual part.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean. Rating capture is declared, so it shows up in review.”

beats.label: Compile it and check it
beats.cue: “--check: GREEN, gated at the declared credentials.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the declared credentials gate

beats.label: Type the feedback block
beats.cue: “Where the reaction lands, and how long it's kept. Ratings are user data — say so in the spec.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Retention on a feedback store is a compliance question, not a tuning knob.”

groups.title: Beat 2 · the two things a user can give you

beats.label: Read the rate contract
beats.cue: “Thumbs and stars are cheap and coarse. --turn targets one turn instead of the last.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “The default target is the last assistant turn — the one the user just reacted to.”

beats.label: Read the feedback contract
beats.cue: “And the expensive, valuable one: free text. 'always cite the file you read' is worth a hundred thumbs.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Text is what the distill step turns into a grader.”

beats.label: Read the distill contract
beats.cue: “--graders-out is the part people miss: distilling writes the dataset AND the graders to score it with.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Ratings in, an eval suite out. That's the conversion this recipe exists to explain.”

beats.label: Run the agent
beats.cue: [needs-key] “First you need a session with a turn worth reacting to.”

verify.note: interactive REPL; needs a model credential

beats.label: Ask it something
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Then judge the answer honestly — the loop is only as good as the rating.”
beats.text: Summarise what this repository is for.

beats.label: Exit
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell.

beats.label: Rate it down with a reason
beats.cue: [needs-key] “A thumbs-down plus a sentence. The sentence is the part that becomes a grader.”
beats.command: crewhaus feedback --session <session-id> --text "always cite the file you read"

verify.note: needs a real session id from the run above

beats.label: Distill it
beats.cue: [needs-key] “3 rated turns → 3 samples, plus a graders file derived from what people actually complained about.”

verify.note: the --judge pass is billed model calls

beats.label: Eval against your own users' judgement
beats.cue: [needs-key] “The dataset is your users. That's a better benchmark than any public one.”

verify.note: needs the distilled dataset and a model credential

beats.label: Optimize against the ratings
beats.cue: [needs-key] “--ratings all closes the loop the recipe opened with.”

beats.label: Read the whole loop
beats.cue: “run → rate → distill → eval → optimize. Five verbs, and none of them is 'guess'.”
